hero.title: Properties of Laser
hero.lead: A laser beam has four fundamental properties that set it apart from every ordinary light source: monochromaticity, directionality, coherence, and brightness.

objectives: List the four fundamental properties of laser light.
Distinguish a laser beam from ordinary light in terms of monochromaticity, directionality, coherence, and brightness.
Calculate the difference in radiant intensity between a laser source and an ordinary light source of the same power.

content.heading: 💡 6-2 Properties of Laser
content.html: A laser beam has the following fundamental properties:

content.label: 📌 1. Monochromaticity (Single Wavelength) Monochromatic
content.html: The laser is distinguished by an optical purity that surpasses any other source, unlike an ordinary light source whose emission spans many colors (many wavelengths) at once. See Figure 6-2.

content.caption: Figure 6-2: Ordinary light disperses into a spectrum of colors through a prism, while a laser beam remains a single color

content.label: 📌 2. Directionality Directionality
content.html: Laser beams travel great distances as nearly parallel bundles with very little divergence, whereas the light from an ordinary lamp or the sun spreads out randomly in every direction. See Figure 6-3.
extraHtml: If a sufficiently intense laser beam were aimed at the Moon from a distance of roughly 384,000 km from Earth's surface, it would illuminate a spot on the Moon's surface no more than about 1 km across, whereas if ordinary light were sent — hypothetically — and reached the Moon's surface, the illuminated spot's diameter would reach roughly 4,376 km.

content.label: 📌 3. Coherence Coherency
content.html: Laser waves are identical in phase, direction, and energy, which allows the waves to interfere constructively with one another. See Figure 6-4.

content.label: 📌 4. Brightness Brightness
content.html: Laser light has an extremely high brilliance and brightness, exceeding the brightness of sunlight by a factor of a million, as a result of concentrating the laser's emitted energy into a narrow, low-divergence beam. See Figure 6-5.

content.problemHtml: A 100-watt tungsten lamp has a radiant intensity of about (2000 watt/cm²), while a laser of the same power (100 watt) has a radiant intensity of about (\(2\times10^{9}\ \text{watt/cm}^2\)). Compare the two intensities.
content.label: 📝 Example (1)

given: \( I_{\text{tungsten}} = 2000\ \text{watt/cm}^2 \) — the radiant intensity of the tungsten lamp
\( I_{\text{laser}} = 2\times10^{9}\ \text{watt/cm}^2 \) — the radiant intensity of the laser at the same power
solution.required: Calculate how many times greater the laser's radiant intensity is than that of the ordinary tungsten lamp.

steps.note: We calculate the ratio of the laser's radiant intensity to the tungsten lamp's radiant intensity

solution.final: ✓ The laser's radiant intensity is a million (\(10^6\)) times greater than the radiant intensity of the ordinary tungsten lamp at the same power
solution.label: Detailed Solution

content.svgAriaLabel: Simulation of laser directionality versus ordinary light
content.sectionHeading: 🕹️ Interactive simulation: Directionality — laser vs. ordinary light
content.descriptionHtml: Choose a light source type and observe the difference in the size of the light spot on a distant screen — just like the example of sending light to the surface of the Moon.

labels.captionLaser: Laser beam: a nearly parallel bundle with very little divergence, so the light spot on the distant screen stays extremely narrow (as in the Moon example: a diameter no more than 1 km).
labels.captionOrdinary: Ordinary light: spreads out randomly in every direction, so the light spot on the distant screen becomes very wide (as in the Moon example: a diameter reaching 4,376 km).

questions.question: The property whereby a laser beam remains a single color that does not disperse through a prism is called:
questions.explain: Monochromaticity means the laser has optical purity (a single color), unlike ordinary light, which spans many wavelengths.

questions.question: The property whereby laser waves are identical in phase, direction, and energy is called:
questions.explain: Coherence (coherency) is the identity of laser waves in phase, direction, and energy, which allows them to interfere constructively.

questions.question: Sending a laser beam to the surface of the Moon (384,000 km) produces a light spot whose diameter does not exceed:
questions.explain: Because of the laser beam's high directionality, the illuminated spot on the Moon's surface does not exceed 1 km in diameter, whereas with ordinary light it would reach roughly 4376 km.

questions.question: The laser's radiant intensity exceeds that of a tungsten lamp of the same power by a factor of:
questions.explain: As in the solved example: \(2\times10^9 \div 2000 = 10^6\), so the laser's intensity is a million times greater.

summary.heading: 📋 Lesson Summary
items: Monochromaticity: optical purity of a single color that does not disperse, unlike light with many wavelengths.
Directionality: nearly parallel, low-divergence beams that reach great distances (Moon example: 1 km for the laser vs. 4376 km for ordinary light).
Coherence: identity of phase, direction, and energy between the waves, so they interfere constructively.
Brightness: extremely high radiant intensity (a million times greater than a tungsten lamp of the same power) from concentrating energy into a narrow beam.
